Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 1800000, max 7200000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

    DIMENSIONS,

    ))

input.description: 探索 ImageFolder 掃描邏輯
input.prompt:
在 /Users/pc035860/code/cee（Swift macOS 圖片檢視器）做 medium 深度唯讀探索。目標：評估「自動 join 巢狀資料夾所有圖片」（遞迴把子資料夾圖片合併成一個平面清單）要改哪裡。
請回報（附 file:line）：
1. ImageFolder 的定義、init(folderURL:)、init(fileURL:)（或類似）、BFS 子資料夾探索（最多 2 層）的完整邏輯
2. 圖片排序方式（natural sort? 檔名? 是否只比檔名而非路徑）、ImageItem 結構（有哪些欄位、是否 Sendable、是否以 url 為 identity）
3. currentIndex 與 index 的使用方式、依賴「同一個資料夾」假設的地方（例如 deletingLastPathComponent、用檔名找 index、刪除/移動檔案、重新整理）
4. 是否有檔案系統監看（DispatchSource/FSEvents/NSFilePresenter）或 refresh/reload 邏輯
5. 刪除/移到垃圾桶/重新命名/Reveal in Finder 等檔案操作對 ImageFolder 的影響
只回報事實與位置，不要改檔案。

input.description: 探索 loadFolder 與開檔流程
input.prompt:
在 /Users/pc035860/code/cee（Swift macOS 圖片檢視器）做 medium 深度唯讀探索。目標：評估「自動 join 巢狀資料夾所有圖片」功能涉及的開檔流程與設定。
請回報（附 file:line）：
1. Finder open / 拖放 / File>Open 到 ImageWindowController.createWindow、ImageViewController.loadFolder 的完整流程；開啟單一檔案 vs 開啟資料夾兩條路徑如何建立 ImageFolder

3. 選單建構（Navigation / View / Go 選單）如何新增 toggle item、validateMenuItem 的寫法，以 reuseWindow 或其他 bool 設定為範例
4. 多視窗去重（dedupe by folder path）的邏輯，會不會受遞迴影響
5. createWindow 的 presizedContentSize / imageHeaderSize 預先設定視窗尺寸流程是否依賴 folder 內容
只回報事實與位置，不要改檔案。

## 1. 開檔流程（Finder open / 拖放 / File>Open → createWindow / loadFolder）

**`ImageWindowController.open(with:)` 的分流** `Cee/Controllers/ImageWindowController.swift:36-50`
- 一律呼叫 `ImageFolder(containing: url)`，沒有資料夾判斷。

- 否則呼叫 `createWindow(with: folder)`。
- `openEmpty()` `:22-33` 在復用時只把既有視窗帶到前景，不載入。

**`createWindow(with:)`** `ImageWindowController.swift:53-129`

## 1. 開檔流程（Finder open / 拖放 / File>Open → createWindow / loadFolder）

**入口 A：Finder open、File>Open**
- Finder open：`AppDelegate.application(_:open:)` `Cee/App/AppDelegate.swift:25-35`，逐個呼叫 `ImageWindowController.open(with:)`。
- File>Open：`AppDelegate.openFile` `AppDelegate.swift:51-58`，`NSOpenPanel` 設 `canChooseDirectories = false`，只接受單一檔案，然後呼叫 `open(with:)`。
- 選單項目 `menu.file.open`（⌘O）掛在 `AppDelegate.swift:80-82`。

**入口 B：拖放到視窗或空白狀態**
- 拖放最終進入 `ImageViewController.handleDrop` `Cee/Controllers/ImageViewController.swift:2056-2088`。來源有 `scrollViewDidReceiveDrop`（2052）與 `emptyStateViewDidReceiveDrop`（2256）。
- 資料夾：直接走 `loadFolderAndSetTitle(imageFolderFromDrop)`（2060-2062）。
- 檔案：若父資料夾與目前 `folder.folderURL` 相同且找得到該檔，只切換 `currentIndex`，不重掃（2065-2084）；否則同樣走 `imageFolderFromDrop`（2087）。
- `imageFolderFromDrop` `ImageViewController.swift:2035-2043` 依 `URLFilter.isDirectory` 分支：資料夾用 `ImageFolder(folderURL:)`，檔案用 `ImageFolder(containing:)`。

**`ImageWindowController.open(with:)` 的分流** `Cee/Controllers/ImageWindowController.swift:36-50`
- 一律呼叫 `ImageFolder(containing: url)`，沒有資料夾判斷。
- 若 `settings.reuseWindow` 為真且存在 `current` 視窗，呼叫 `vc.loadFolder(folder)`、`updateTitle`、`makeKeyAndOrderFront`。
- 否則呼叫 `createWindow(with: folder)`。
- `openEmpty()` `:22-33` 在復用時只把既有視窗帶到前景，不載入。

**`createWindow(with:)`** `ImageWindowController.swift:53-129`
- 讀取 `ViewerSettings.load()`，建立 `ImageViewController(folder:)`，建立 `NSWindow`，設定 `contentViewController`。
- 之後依設定決定尺寸（見第 5 點），最後 `showWindow`、`ensureUsableWindowSize`（`:259`）、`setupWindowObservers`、`updateTitle`。

**`ImageViewController.loadFolder`** `ImageViewController.swift:191-221`
- 重置 `isManualZoom`、清 `imageSizeCache`，呼叫 `loadFolderDualPageSettings()`（`:201`），再依 continuousScroll / dualPage / 單頁選擇載入方式。
- 首次建立視窗時，folder 由 `init(folder:)` 注入（`:74-77`），實際載入發生在 `viewDidAppear`（`:120-146`）。`viewDidAppear` 也會呼叫 `loadFolderDualPageSettings()`（`:136`）。

**兩條建立 ImageFolder 的路徑** `Cee/Models/ImageFolder.swift`
- 單一檔案 `init(containing:)` `:21-42`：`folderURL = fileURL.deletingLastPathComponent()`，掃描父資料夾，再用 `resolvingSymlinksInPath().path` 找到該檔的 index。PDF 會讀取上次頁碼（`:30-34`）。**不會遞迴，也不會搜尋子資料夾。**
- 資料夾 `init(folderURL:)` `:48-61`：`folderURL` 即參數本身，掃描頂層。若頂層無圖，呼叫 `findFirstSubfolderWithImages(in:maxDepth: 2)`（`:53-58`），以 BFS 找第一個含圖的子資料夾，並**改寫 `self.folderURL` 為找到的子資料夾**。這是目前唯一的「向下搜尋」邏輯，且只在頂層為空時觸發，只取一個子資料夾，不會合併。
- 共用 `scanFolder()` `:63-90`：只掃頂層（`.skipsHiddenFiles`），依 UTType 過濾，PDF 展開為每頁一個 `ImageItem`。

**Info.plist**：`Cee/App/Info.plist` 的 `CFBundleDocumentTypes` 只宣告影像 UTI（jpeg/png/tiff/heic/heif/gif/webp/bmp），沒有 `public.folder`。推論：Finder「開啟方式」與 Dock 拖資料夾到 app 圖示，系統不一定會把資料夾送進 `application(_:open:)`，目前實際主要是視窗內拖放。

## 2. ViewerSettings 與 per-folder 覆寫

**結構** `Cee/Models/ViewerSettings.swift`
- `struct ViewerSettings: Codable` `:3`。欄位都有預設值。
- 與本功能相關的欄位：`dualPageEnabled`（`:66`，預設 false）、`firstPageIsCover`（`:67`）、`readingDirection`（`:75`，預設 `.rightToLeft`）、`duoPageRTLNavigation`（`:77`）、`singlePageRTLNavigation`（`:79`）、`continuousScrollEnabled`（`:89`）、`continuousScrollGap`（`:91`）、`reuseWindow`（`:53`，預設 true）、`lastWindowWidth/Height`（`:54-55`，nil）、`resizeWindowAutomatically`（`:51`）、`alwaysFitOnOpen`（`:10`，預設 true）、`showStatusBar`（`:62`）、`clickToTurnPage`（`:85`）。
- `isManualZoom`（`:7`）刻意不解碼（`:101`），屬 session 狀態。

**Codable 解碼** `:95-128`
- 自訂 `init(from:)`，每個欄位都用 `(try? c.decode(...)) ?? d.xxx`，`d = ViewerSettings()` 作為預設來源。也就是缺欄位或型別錯誤時退回預設值，舊資料相容。
- 例外：`lastWindowWidth/Height` 直接 `try?` 不帶預設（`:113-114`）；`continuousScrollGap` 用 `max(0, ...)`（`:127`）。
- 注意：`ViewerSettings` 沒有 `dualPage` 的 per-folder 欄位，這些是 ViewerSettings 的全域欄位。

**持久化**
- 全域設定：`UserDefaults.standard`，key 為 `"CeeViewerSettings"`（`:131`），`load()` `:133-138`、`save()` `:140-144`，皆為 JSON。
- `reuseWindow` 切換：`AppDelegate.toggleReuseWindow` `AppDelegate.swift:235-239`。

**Per-folder dual-page 覆寫**（資料夾路徑作為 key）
- 結構 `FolderDualPageSettings` `ImageViewController.swift:606-628`，欄位為 `dualPageEnabled`、`firstPageIsCover`、`readingDirection`、`duoPageRTLNavigation`。其中 `duoPageRTLNavigation` 缺欄位時預設 true（`:626`）。
- **key**：`"dualPage.settings.\(folder.folderURL.path)"`，寫入於 `saveFolderDualPageSettings` `:630-642`（key 在 `:632`），讀取於 `loadFolderDualPageSettings` `:644-655`（key 在 `:646`）。
- 因此 key 來自 `ImageFolder.folderURL`，**不是檔案路徑**。若 `folderURL` 被 BFS 改寫為子資料夾，key 會變成子資料夾路徑。
- 寫入點：`toggleDualPage` `:1217-1224`、`togglePageOffset` `:1227-1235`、`toggleReadingDirection` `:1353-1358`、`toggleDuoPageRTLNavigation` `:1362-1367`。`toggleSinglePageRTLNavigation` 不寫入 per-folder。
- 讀取點：`viewDidAppear` `:136`、`loadFolder` `:201`。讀到就直接覆寫全域 `settings` 的四個欄位（`:650-653`）。
- PDF 頁碼另有 key：`"pdf.lastPage.\(url.path)"`，見 `ImageFolder.swift:171` 與 `ImageViewController.swift:600-601`，以檔案路徑為 key。

## 3. 選單建構與 toggle 寫法

**選單建構** 全部在 `AppDelegate.setupMenuBar()` `AppDelegate.swift:62-223`
- `makeItem(title, action, key)` `:227-231`：`item.target = nil`，經 responder chain 分派到 first responder（通常是 `ImageViewController`）。
- Navigation 選單 `:140-198`：Reading mode 組 `:146-155`（`toggleDualPage` 在 `:147`，`k` 鍵）；Navigation settings 組 `:159-164`（`toggleClickToTurnPage` `:163`，`toggleContinuousScroll` `:164`）；子選單 `:166-192`；Quick Grid 組 `:196-198`。
- View 選單 `:89-138`，`toggleStatusBar` 在 `:138`。
- Go 選單 `:200-208`，只有上下張與首末張，沒有 toggle。
- Window 選單 `:210-220`：`reuseWindow` 項目在 `:218-220`，target 設為 `self`（AppDelegate），**這是唯一 target 指向 AppDelegate 的 toggle**，其餘都是 nil。

**toggle 方法寫法**
- ImageViewController 版本（大部分）：`@objc func toggleX(_ sender: Any? = nil)`，內容為 `settings.x.toggle()` → `settings.save()` → 必要時更新 UI。例：`toggleClickToTurnPage` `ImageViewController.swift:1380-1383`、`toggleContinuousScroll` `:1386-`、`toggleDualPage` `:1217-1226`。
- AppDelegate 版本：`@objc func toggleReuseWindow(_ sender: Any?)` `AppDelegate.swift:235-239`，只做 load → toggle → save，沒有 UI 更新。

**validateMenuItem 寫法**
- AppDelegate 版本 `AppDelegate.swift:243-250`：`guard menuItem.action == #selector(toggleReuseWindow(_:)) else { return true }`，然後 `menuItem.state = settings.reuseWindow ? .on : .off`，回傳 true。`AppDelegate` 宣告 `NSMenuItemValidation`（`:4`）。
- ImageViewController 版本 `ImageViewController.swift:1658-` 以 `switch menuItem.action` 集中處理，例如 `toggleClickToTurnPage` 設 `.state` 並回傳 `!isContinuous`（`:1747-1749` 附近），`toggleDualPage` 回傳 `!isContinuous`（`:1735-1738`），`toggleStatusBar` 會改 `menuItem.title`（`:1712-1716`）。我未讀到該 switch 的結尾（約 1760 行之後）。
- 新增 toggle 的一般步驟：(a) `ViewerSettings` 加欄位、加 `init(from:)` 解碼；(b) `AppDelegate.setupMenuBar` 加 `makeItem`；(c) 在 `ImageViewController` 加 `@objc toggleX`；(d) 在 `ImageViewController.validateMenuItem` 的 switch 加 case；(e) 兩個 xcstrings / `Localizable.strings`（`en.lproj`、`zh-Hant.lproj`）加字串，例如 `menu.window.reuseWindow` `zh-Hant.lproj/Localizable.strings:77`。

## 4. 多視窗去重與遞迴的影響

**去重位置**：`AppDelegate.application(_:open:)` `AppDelegate.swift:26-31`
- 去重鍵是 `url.deletingLastPathComponent().path`，也就是**父資料夾路徑**，並保留每個父資料夾的第一個 URL。
- 這個去重只發生在一次 open 事件的 URL 陣列內，不會查詢既有視窗。
- 去重後逐個呼叫 `ImageWindowController.open(with:)`。在復用模式下，每次呼叫都會 `loadFolder` 覆寫同一個視窗，所以最終顯示的是最後一個 folder。
- `ImageWindowController` 本身沒有「依 folder path 找既有視窗」的邏輯。`current` 只取 key/main/最後一個視窗（`ImageWindowController.swift:14-17`）。

**對遞迴的影響（推論，需驗證）**
- 去重鍵是父路徑，與子資料夾深度無關。若使用者一次開 `/a/b/` 與 `/a/c/` 兩個資料夾，兩者父路徑皆為 `/a`，第二個會被丟掉。這是既有的 bug 疑慮：`deletingLastPathComponent` 對資料夾 URL 語意錯誤。目前 Info.plist 未宣告資料夾型別，所以觸發條件較窄。
- 若新功能讓同一棵樹底下的多個檔案被展開，各檔的父路徑不同（`/root/x/a.jpg`、`/root/y/b.jpg`），去重不會合併它們，會連續呼叫 `open(with:)`。在復用模式下最後一次會覆寫前面的結果。
- `ImageFolder.init(containing:)` 沒有遞迴，`init(folderURL:)` 只有頂層掃描加 BFS 找第一個子資料夾，因此目前沒有「收集全部巢狀圖片」的路徑。

## 5. createWindow 的預先尺寸流程是否依賴 folder 內容

`ImageWindowController.createWindow` `:53-129`，有三段尺寸邏輯：
1. **連續捲動模式** `:56-60`：固定寬度 `Constants.continuousScrollNewWindowContentWidth`，高度為 `minWindowContentHeight`，**不依賴 folder**。之後 `:81-96` 用螢幕 `visibleFrame` 展開高度，也不依賴 folder。
2. **一般模式** `:62`：`savedOrDefaultWindowSize()`（`:132-141`，取 `lastWindowWidth/Height` 或螢幕 80%），不依賴 folder。
3. **預先依圖片縮放** `:97-121`：條件為 `!settings.dualPageEnabled`、`(alwaysFitOnOpen || resizeWindowAutomatically)`，且 `folder?.currentImage?.url` 存在，並能讀到 `ImageLoader.imageHeaderSize(at:)`（`ImageLoader.swift:228`）。
   - **依賴 folder**：只取 `folder.currentImage`，也就是 `images[currentIndex]` 的第一張（`ImageFolder.swift:179`）。`folder` 為 nil 或無圖時跳過，視窗維持預設尺寸。
   - 計算由 `presizedContentSize`（`:165-178`）完成，依 `FittingCalculator` 與狀態列高度換算。
   - 讀的是 `ViewerSettings.load()` 的**全域** `dualPageEnabled`，而非 per-folder 覆寫。原因是 per-folder 覆寫要到 `viewDidAppear`（`ImageViewController.swift:136`）才套用，晚於 `createWindow`。推論：若某資料夾 per-folder 設為雙頁，而全域為單頁，預先尺寸仍會依單頁計算。
4. **之後的修正**：`ensureUsableWindowSize` `:259-270` 只在 `async` 中檢查視窗是否小於最小尺寸，不讀 folder。

`ImageViewController.openFitViewport` `ImageViewController.swift:657-666` 也會在載入時用螢幕尺寸重算 fit，與上述預先尺寸是獨立的第二條路徑。

- 既有測試：`CeeTests/ImageFolderSubfolderSearchTests.swift` 覆蓋 `findFirstSubfolderWithImages`（`:165`、`:175`）；`CeeTests/ImageWindowControllerTests.swift` 與 `ImageViewControllerTests.swift:193` 也會呼叫 `loadFolder`。

- `CLAUDE.md:149` 說明 multi-file open 以資料夾路徑去重，與上面程式碼一致。</result>

開檔與設定那路回來了，那兩份 specs 也確認過，跟這個功能無關（一份只是這次 session 的 handover）。顯示層那路還沒到~

**開檔流程**
- 開單一檔案走 `ImageFolder(containing:)`，只掃父資料夾，完全不看子資料夾（`ImageFolder.swift:21-42`）。
- 開資料夾（只有視窗內拖放）走 `init(folderURL:)`。
- File > Open 的 `NSOpenPanel` 設了 `canChooseDirectories = false`（`AppDelegate.swift:51-58`）。
- `Info.plist` 的 `CFBundleDocumentTypes` 沒宣告 `public.folder`。所以你的範例路徑，目前只能靠拖資料夾進視窗打開。

**會踩到的坑**
- **per-folder dual-page 設定**：key 是 `"dualPage.settings.\(folder.folderURL.path)"`（`ImageViewController.swift:632`、`:646`）。合併模式下 `folderURL` 要保持你給的根目錄，這個 key 才會穩定。
- **視窗預先縮放**：只取 `folder.currentImage` 那一張的 header（`ImageWindowController.swift:97-121`），不受合併影響。
- **既有 bug**：`AppDelegate.swift:26-31` 的去重用 `deletingLastPathComponent()`，對資料夾 URL 語意不對。一次開 `/a/b` 和 `/a/c` 會被誤判成同一個。這是開資料夾入口多了之後才會咬人的老問題，順手可修。

**加設定開關要動的地方**（跟 `reuseWindow` 或 `clickToTurnPage` 同款，約 5 處）：
1. `ViewerSettings` 加欄位和解碼。
2. `AppDelegate.setupMenuBar` 加選單項。
3. `ImageViewController` 加 `@objc toggleX`。
4. `validateMenuItem` 的 switch 加 case。
5. en 和 zh-Hant 的 `Localizable.strings` 加字串。

**討論點**
1. **預設行為**：頂層有圖也合併子資料夾，還是維持現狀、只在頂層無圖時才合併？
2. **開關位置**：全域設定（Navigation 選單），或是開資料夾時才觸發？後者不用加設定。
3. **排序鍵**：用相對路徑 natural sort，讓同一子資料夾的圖連在一起。我建議這個，混排通常不是你要的。
4. **遞迴深度**：不限，還是設上限？

等顯示層回報後，我整理成一份建議方案給你選。

## 1. Quick Grid（QuickGridView）

**清單來源**
- 開啟時：`/Users/pc035860/code/cee/Cee/Controllers/ImageViewController.swift:1339` 呼叫 `grid.configure(items: folder.images, currentIndex: folder.currentIndex, loader: loader)`，來源是 `ImageFolder.images`。

- 沒有資料夾概念，也沒有假設同資料夾。`ImageItem`（`/Users/pc035860/code/cee/Cee/Models/ImageItem.swift:3-17`）只有 `url` 與 `pdfPageIndex`。
- 格子選取回呼：`ImageViewController.swift:2268-2285` 直接設 `folder.currentIndex = index`，合併清單時仍然成立。

**檔名與縮圖顯示**
- 檔名：`QuickGridCell.swift:70` 使用 `item.fileName`，`ImageItem.swift:14-17` 為 `url.lastPathComponent`（PDF 加 "— Page N"）。
- 格子沒有 `toolTip`，也沒有第二行路徑。同名檔案在不同子資料夾中會顯示完全相同的文字，無法區分。
- 縮圖載入在 `QuickGridView.swift:1412-1460`，呼叫 `loader.loadThumbnail(at: item.url, maxSize:)`。

**Cache key 與 generationID**
- 格子層快取以 **index（Int）為 key**：`gridThumbnails: [Int: NSImage]`（`QuickGridView.swift:369`）、`gridThumbnailSizes`（`:371`）、`thumbnailTasks: [Int: Task]`（`:379`）。
- `generationID` 是 folder 變更計數器，不是 URL（`QuickGridView.swift:402`）。`clearCache()` 在 `:1380-1383` 遞增它，並清空格子快取。
- stale write 防護在 `:667-674`（prefetch）與 `:1439-1446`（loadThumbnail）。
- `configure()` 本身不會遞增 generationID，也不清 `gridThumbnails`。
- `ImageViewController.swift:215-216`（loadFolder 路徑）會先 `clearCache()` 再 `configure()`，這條路徑安全。
- 但同資料夾路徑 `ImageViewController.swift:2079` 只呼叫 `configure()`，沒有 `clearCache()`。若合併後清單在既有 grid 實例中被換掉，會沿用以 index 為 key 的舊縮圖，造成錯位。
- ImageLoader 層的 thumbnail cache 才是以 URL 為 key（見第 4 節）。

**其他假設與效能**
- 縮圖快取上限以 index 距離淘汰：`QuickGridView.swift:691-701`。
- 中斷範圍計算使用 `items.count`（`:599`、`:652`、`:899`），都是 O(1) 或 O(range)。
- `sampleMedianAspectRatio`（`:1019-1036`）只取前 50 張非 PDF 的 header，並且在主執行緒同步讀取。合併後仍只代表清單前段。
- `isCurrentImage` 以 index 比對（`:1480-1481`）。

## 2. Continuous Scroll 與 Dual Page

**清單與 index 取得**
- Continuous 入口：`ImageViewController.swift:1425` `configureContinuousScrollView()`，把 `targetIndex = folder.currentIndex` 交給 `onPreloadComplete`。
- `ContinuousScrollContentView.swift:152-213` 的 `configure(with:)` 捕獲 `folder.images`，並在 `:184-201` 建立 TaskGroup。
- **效能風險：一次為所有項目建立 child task**，每個 task 呼叫 `loader.getImageSize(for:)`（`/Users/pc035860/code/cee/Cee/Services/ImageLoader.swift:243-255`）。這是 actor 方法，因此所有 header 讀取會在 ImageLoader actor 上序列化，底層是同步的 `imageHeaderSize`（`ImageLoader.swift:228-240`）。
- 在所有 header 讀完前，佈局不會開始（`ContinuousScrollContentView.swift:203-211`）。N 很大時首次顯示會被延遲。
- 無法取得尺寸時使用預設比例（`:187-191`）。

**yOffsets 與佈局**
- `recalculateLayout()`（`ContinuousScrollContentView.swift:222-250`）每次都重建整個 `scaledHeights`（`:232`）與 `yOffsets`（`:236-242`），是 O(N)。
- 觸發來源是 `containerWidth` didSet（`:25-27`）與 `imageSpacing` didSet（`:30-32`），經 `relayoutSlots()`（`:35-74`）。視窗縮放時每一步都會觸發 O(N) 重算。
- `recalculateLayout` 內有 `NSLog`（`:247`），在縮放熱路徑中會產生日誌。
- 二分搜尋的 `calculateCurrentIndex`（`:552-574`）與 `calculateVisibleRange`（`:302-316`）已是 O(log N)，沒有問題。
- `manageSlotViews` 的 `isSlotActive` 是對 `activeSlots` 的線性搜尋（`:327-329`），但 active 數量很小。

**Prefetch 與 ImageLoader**
- `triggerPrefetch`（`ContinuousScrollContentView.swift:420-451`）把整個 `folder.images` 傳給 `loader.updateCache`（`ImageLoader.swift:354-412`）。Array 是 CoW，不會複製，但 `updateCache` 會每次過濾整個 cache dictionary。
- `:446` 傳入的是 `visibleRange.lowerBound`，不是真正的 currentIndex。

**Status bar 讀取**
- `ImageViewController.swift:266-283` 以 `continuousScrollContentView?.imageSizes[safe:]` 取得尺寸。`imageSizes` 宣告在 `ContinuousScrollContentView.swift:16`。

**Dual Page（loadSpread 與 imageSizeCache）**
- `loadSpread` 在 `ImageViewController.swift:478-` 使用 `folder.currentSpread`，spreads 是預先算好的陣列。
- `imageSizeCache: [Int: CGSize]` 宣告在 `ImageViewController.swift:50`，以 index 為 key。
  - 只在 `resolveLayoutSize`（`:586-591`）中，當頁面被實際顯示時才寫入。
  - `loadFolder` 會清空（`:200`）。
  - 重建 spreads 時傳給 `SpreadManager.buildSpreads` 的 provider 讀取這個 cache（`:1241-1245`）。
- **結果**：`SpreadManager.isWidePage`（`/Users/pc035860/code/cee/Cee/Models/SpreadManager.swift`）對未知尺寸視為 portrait（`nil` 回傳 false）。spreads 只在 `rebuildSpreadsAndReload`（`:1238-1248`）時重算，因此未被顯示過的非 PDF 寬頁會被當成直頁配對。
- `rebuildSpreadsAndReload` 在 `:207`（loadFolder）、`:138`、`:1223`（toggleDualPage）、`:1234`（togglePageOffset）呼叫。
- `prepopulatePDFPageSizes()`（`:1250-1274`）每次重建都會遍歷**全部 N 個項目**，並為每個 PDF 開 `CGPDFDocument`（`:1253-1273`），是 O(N) 同步工作。
- `SpreadManager.buildSpreads`（`SpreadManager.swift:17-45`）只看相鄰 index 配對，**沒有資料夾邊界檢查**。合併多資料夾後，最後一張 A 資料夾圖片與第一張 B 資料夾圖片可能被配成同一個 spread。
- `spreadIndex`（`SpreadManager.swift` 的 `firstIndex` 線性搜尋）與 `syncSpreadIndex`（`ImageFolder.swift:259-261`）在 dual 模式下每次 `goNext`/`goPrevious` 都會執行，對數千張仍可接受。

**ImageFolder 掃描的效能風險（合併前就存在，遞迴後會放大）**

- `findFirstSubfolderWithImages`（`:99-126`）使用 `queue.removeFirst()`，是 O(n²) 的小問題。

- **視窗標題**：`/Users/pc035860/code/cee/Cee/Controllers/ImageWindowController.swift:531-552`。
  - 狀態列隱藏時，標題是 `item.url.lastPathComponent (i/N)`（`:547`）。

模型層、Grid、Continuous Scroll、Dual Page 都是平面 `[ImageItem]` 加 index，`ImageLoader` 的 cache 又都以 URL 為 key，同名檔不會衝突。核心只有一處：`ImageFolder` 的掃描。你的範例路徑（根目錄 15 個子資料夾、共 344 張圖）規模很小，效能不是問題。

- **Dual page 跨資料夾配對**：`SpreadManager.buildSpreads` 沒有資料夾邊界檢查，A 資料夾最後一張可能和 B 資料夾第一張配成一頁。

Base directory for this skill: /Users/pc035860/.claude/skills/verify-code-change

# Verify Code Change — orchestrator-delegated verification protocol

This skill defines the full verification protocol for **Tier 3** code changes delegated by an orchestrator that explicitly adopts the Tier 0–3 model, including the discord-channel and Fable orchestrators. It lives in user scope so cross-project workers can invoke it by skill name without embedding an installation path in their brief.

## When to invoke

Invoke only when the parent explicitly classified the task as **Tier 3**. Do not invoke merely because source files, types, schemas, or runtime config changed.

If execution reveals new evidence that makes the assigned Tier 0–2 classification materially unsafe, pause the affected work and report that evidence to the parent for reclassification. Do not self-upgrade or start this protocol without a revised Tier 3 brief.

## Tier 3 protocol — strict sequence: L1/L2 → simplify gate → Dimension B → deslop → L3

Self-verifying code you just wrote is unreliable: bias from authorship hides spec deviation, edge cases, and quality issues. The two failure modes need different kinds of independence:

- **Dimension A — Runtime verification**: does the code actually run and behave correctly? Needs a **fresh-context executor** (a subagent you spawn).
- **Dimension B — Static code review**: does the diff match the spec and meet the quality bar? Needs a **different model** — the Codex process that `review-loop` drives — which you invoke from your own context. Listed A-first for concept, executed B-first — see the order below.

Neither dimension substitutes for the other. The required order is:

1. Run L1 and L2.
2. Assess the simplify gate and run it only when justified.
3. If the simplify pass changed code, rerun L1 and L2.
4. Run Dimension B inline in your own context until the loop terminates —
   blockers cleared, or you stop with blockers outstanding (cap: 3 review
   rounds + 1 confirm-only round) and close out per the **final-round rule**
   in B1: fix, confirm-only round, survivors reported unresolved. Commit
   only after Dimension B has terminated — after the confirm round when one
   ran, otherwise after the zero-blocker reviewer response — never mid-loop.
   Prefer committing after step 5 so the deslop pass does not produce a
   second, comment-only commit.
   If it changed code, rerun L1 and L2.
5. Run the mandatory `deslop` pass (comments only, own context, no gate) on
   the cumulative diff — see the Deslop pass section. If it changed
   anything, rerun L1 and L2.
6. Only then spawn L3 against that final diff. **Never run Dimension B and
   L3 concurrently**: review fixes land in the working tree and trigger the
   dev server's HMR / rebuild, which interrupts the E2E run and makes its
   verdict meaningless. Any code change after L3 starts invalidates both
   that L3 run and the completed Dimension B review: rerun L3, and rerun
   Dimension B unless the fix is confined to what the L3 report itself
   named.

## Dimension A — Runtime verification

Layered: L1 → L2 → L3. L3 is the gate.

| Layer | Check | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | Build / type-check / lint passes | Direct, in your own context (deterministic; `bun x tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, etc.) |
| L2 | Unit / mock tests pass | Direct, in your own context (deterministic; `bun test`, `pytest`, etc.) |
| L3 | Real end-to-end against the actual system | **Fresh-context executor** — see tool-selection table below |

L1 + L2 are deterministic and self-contained, so running them in your own context is fine. L3 needs a separate executor because it usually spawns long-running processes (servers, browsers, daemons) and because a fresh perceptual frame is what catches "compiles but doesn't actually do what the spec said."

### L3 execution protocol — built-in `verify` skill + driver hints

The fresh-context L3 executor invokes the **built-in `verify` skill** (Claude Code bundled, user-invocable via the Skill tool) as its first step and follows its discipline end-to-end. What that buys us, at zero overlap with the other layers:

- Runtime observation only — the built-in skill itself forbids re-running tests / typecheck, so it never duplicates L1/L2
- At least one adversarial probe (🔍) beyond the happy path — all-✅ steps count as a happy-path replay, not verification
- Captured output (pane dumps, response bodies, screenshots) is the evidence; memory is not
- Strict verdict semantics: PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED / SKIP, no partial pass, when in doubt FAIL

Two known frictions — handle both in the L3 task prompt:

1. The built-in skill re-establishes scope from `git diff` on its own. Pass the diff range in the task prompt anyway; treat its re-derivation as an independent cross-check, not waste.
2. It discovers drivers via repo-local `verifier-*` / `run-*` skills, then falls back to README cold start — it does not know this environment's drivers. Include the driver-hint table below in the task prompt.

Side effect to be aware of: on a cold start the built-in skill persists what it learned as `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md` in the **target repo**. This is desirable (accumulates that repo's build/run recipe for future sessions) but means L3 may write a file into the target project — expect it, don't treat it as scope creep.

### Driver hints by task type (include in the L3 task prompt)

| Task type | Driver |
|---|---|
| Web / UI feature | `/e2e-dev-loop` skill (Agent Browser driver) |
| Terminal / CLI tool / daemon / general shell process | `tmux` pane — start the process, observe stdout/stderr, send keys |
| Verification itself needs a fresh Claude Code agent (e.g. spinning a new `claude` session to receive a channel injection, like discord-channel's bridge) | `agent-remote` skill (agent-deck / herdr) |
| API / library | Call it for real with representative input, observe real output |
| Mixed | Pick the dominant axis; chain tools if necessary |

The table is a prescription, not a suggestion. For Web/UI in particular: do **NOT** hand-write a headless-browser script (Puppeteer / Playwright / raw Chromium) as a substitute — writing your own E2E script in your own context defeats the fresh-perceptual-frame purpose of L3 and re-introduces authorship bias. Use the `e2e-dev-loop` skill, or drive the `agent-browser` CLI (via the `agent-browser` skill) directly when a full dev-loop is overkill. If the prescribed tool is genuinely unavailable (not installed, environment broken), say so in the report and mark L3 accordingly — don't silently downgrade to a hand-rolled script.

### The self-verification trap

`bun test` passing ≠ feature works. Type-check passing ≠ no bugs. Don't conflate L1/L2 with L3 — only L3 against the actual system proves runtime behavior.

## Simplify pass — exceptional, between L2 and Dimension B

After L1 + L2 are green, inspect the diff once. Do not invoke `/simplify` simply because the diff is large or because a reviewer might possibly find something. The pass launches multiple agents, so it needs a concrete reason.

### Assessment gate — look at the diff, then decide

Run `/simplify` only when inspection identifies at least one concrete **structural** signal: duplicated logic that may already have a helper, an awkward new abstraction, visible scar tissue from repeated fixes, or a likely hot-path inefficiency. If there is no named signal, skip silently. Diff size alone is not a signal.

Comment slop is **not** a signal this gate weighs; the mandatory post-review `deslop` step (see the Deslop pass section) handles it unconditionally.

Two categorical skips (not judgment calls):

- Generated code (lockfiles, tool-generated migrations, type stubs)
- Code covered by an explicit do-not-simplify or equivalent guardrail in the
  target repository's `CLAUDE.md` or task brief. Read the target repository's
  applicable instructions; do not derive them relative to this skill's
  installation directory.

When unsure, skip — Dimension B will still catch material quality issues; simplify is an optimizer, not a gate.

### Running it

- Invoke the `simplify` skill on the changed code (scope it to this task's diff, not the whole repo). It covers comment slop too, but that does not replace the mandatory post-review `deslop` step — review fixes land after this pass.
- If the simplify pass made changes: **re-run L1 + L2** before proceeding — a cleanup pass that breaks the build must be caught here, not in L3
- Guardrail check: reject any simplify edit that violates the target
  repository's applicable instructions, even if it "looks cleaner"

Report the simplify pass only if it ran or produced a warning. Do not spend output on a routine skip.

## Dimension B — Static code review

An independent reviewer reads the diff with no authorship bias. Independence comes from the reviewer being a **different model**: Codex in B1, the `fable` model in B2. Adding a Claude subagent of your own around an already-independent reviewer buys nothing. "Different" is measured against whoever **authored** the diff, not against you: when the parent's brief names the implementer, `review-loop` must not be pointed at that route — a Grok-authored diff bars `grok`; a GLM-authored one bars `pi` / `glm` (the `cursor` route is GPT and stays available). Hunts:

- Spec deviation (does the code do what the spec / task brief said?)
- Bugs the author missed (edge cases, error handling, race conditions)
- Quality issues (dead code, missed validation, overengineering)
- Missed requirements from the task brief

### Two valid implementations — pick one

**Option B1 — `review-loop` skill (Codex iterative)** (preferred default)

- Invoke the `review-loop` skill **in your own context** (Skill tool). The Codex CLI process it drives is already the independent reviewer — do not spawn a subagent to run it, and do not tell it "review only, no fixes".
- The loop is: Codex reviews → you validate the findings and apply the fixes yourself → you run the next round against the **same** Codex session. `review-loop` owns the resume mechanics: keep the session id it reports and hand it back on each later round exactly as that skill's instructions say. One Codex session per Dimension B run. Cap at **4 finding-requesting reviewer invocations**: at most 3 review rounds, plus at most 1 confirm-only round (see final-round rule). Clarification re-queries under review-loop's Validate step request no findings and do not count against the cap. Where `review-loop`'s own termination checklist says "all blocking issues fixed → complete", this skill overrides it: completion requires a reviewer response with zero blockers. If review-loop hits Pause Termination (user decision required) and no user is reachable, stop the loop, record the item as unresolved with its `file:line`, and surface the decision to the parent in the Warning line.
- **Final-round rule.** "Resolved" means *the reviewer's last response had zero blocking findings* — not "I applied a fix". Whenever you stop the loop with blockers outstanding — cap reached, budget, or an early stop for any reason — you may fix them, but you must then run exactly **one confirm-only round**: `--resume` the same session with a prompt that lists the fixed items and asks only whether each is now closed — no new findings requested. Anything new it raises anyway is recorded as unresolved, never fixed in this run — except that if it identifies a fix of yours that breaks the build or tests, repair it and rerun L1/L2; that repair does not earn another reviewer round, and the item still reports as unresolved. If the confirm round clears them, report resolved; if it doesn't, or you skip it, every remaining blocker goes into the report as **unresolved** with its `file:line`.
- Per-round scope: from round 2 on, ask the reviewer to re-check the previous round's blockers and any regression the fixes introduced, before it looks for anything new; genuinely new findings are still welcome. From round 3 on you may defer *non-blocking* wording / spec-phrasing nits without fixing them — list them in the report as deferred suggestions. Never downgrade a finding the reviewer marked blocking; that reclassification is the reviewer's call, not yours.
- Spends no Claude budget and brings a genuinely different model's perspective to the diff.
- Subagent-wrapping this loop multiplies the wall clock, because each subagent restarts Codex from a cold read of the diff.

**Option B2 — `code-auditor` subagent** (fallback)

- Only when `review-loop` is genuinely unavailable (Codex CLI not installed, environment broken) — state the reason in the report
- Spawn via Agent tool with `subagent_type: "code-auditor"` and `model: "fable"`, `effort: "high"` (review is a thinking-shaped task)
- Prompt should include: cumulative diff range (e.g. `git diff <base>..<head>` output, or instruction to compute it), task spec / brief, and "find bugs, spec deviations, quality issues; report as a structured list with file:line citations"
- Single pass, returns a finding list

Pick B1 by default. Fall back to B2 only when review-loop is unavailable.

### Spawn budget for this protocol

You are the implementer, not an orchestrator. The subagents this protocol calls for are exactly:

- **L3** — one fresh-context executor (Dimension A). Required.
- **B2 `code-auditor`** — only in the B1-unavailable fallback.
- Whatever `/simplify` spawns internally when the gate says to run it.
- `prompt-reviewer` / `skill-reviewer` when the parent's brief named them.

Everything else — L1, L2, the simplify gate assessment, B1 review-loop, applying fixes, the post-review `deslop` pass, re-running checks — happens in your own context. Finish Dimension B **before** spawning L3 (see the required order above — the two must not overlap, because review fixes trigger HMR and break the E2E run). After spawning L3, wait for it with the blocking `TaskOutput` tool — never with `sleep` / `until` loops in Bash, which only stall until the Bash timeout. Write the report only after L3's verdict is in.

Do not stack B1 and B2 by default. One independent reviewer is sufficient. Add a second reviewer only when the parent explicitly requests it or the first review exposes a security-critical ambiguity it cannot resolve.

### When B is N/A

Generated code (lockfiles, tool-generated migrations, type stubs), pure config edits with no logic, pure formatting changes. State briefly in your report and skip.

## Deslop pass — mandatory, after Dimension B terminates and before L3

Once the review loop has terminated (zero-blocker response, or the confirm round), invoke the `deslop` skill scoped to the task's cumulative diff — in your own context, no subagent. This is not gated by the simplify assessment and is not skipped because the diff "looks clean": the loop's fix rounds are where implementation-phase markers, review-round narration (`R1 blocker`, `per codex round 2`, `reviewer asked for…`), and comments that talk to the reviewer instead of the next reader get written, and the author who just wrote them is the wrong judge of whether they are load-bearing.

- Scope: **comments only** — this instance of `deslop` does not touch code, casts, or defensive checks, whatever the underlying skill's broader categories allow. Non-comment slop you notice here goes into the report as "noticed", not into the working tree; a non-comment edit after Dimension B would need the review re-run. Keep constraints, rationale, and non-obvious behavior; drop anything that narrates the review history or the edit sequence.
- If it changed anything, re-run L1 + L2. A comment-only pass does not invalidate Dimension B's verdict; it runs before L3, so it does not invalidate L3 either.
- Report it in one line only if it removed something or was blocked; a no-op pass gets no output.

## Multi-phase implementation

Run Dimension B, then L3, once against the final cumulative state before the release boundary. Do not repeat the full protocol after every intermediate phase unless that phase ships independently or the parent explicitly requests a phase gate. If verification must be deferred because the current phase is not runnable, say where the final gate will occur.

## Report format to the parent orchestrator

Give the parent enough evidence to make the ship/no-ship decision, without narrating the verification ceremony.

```
Verification: PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED — [strongest runtime observation]; [independent review verdict].
Review: B1 [N] review rounds[ + 1 confirm] — last reviewer response: [K] blocking; unresolved: [none | file:line — 3–8 word description, one per line].
Warning: [include only for a failed, deferred, incomplete check, or unresolved material non-blocking risk].
```

The `Review:` line is mandatory. `[N]` counts review rounds only; add `+ 1 confirm` when the confirm round ran. `[K]` = blocking findings still open in the reviewer's **last** response, including anything it raised unprompted during the confirm round; `[K]` must equal the number of `unresolved` entries **that came from reviewer findings**. Items recorded from a review-loop Pause Termination are listed separately as `pending decision: file:line — …`, are excluded from `[K]`, and make Verification BLOCKED, not FAIL. For Option B2 write `Review: B2 code-auditor single pass — [K] blocking; unresolved: [...]`; when Dimension B is N/A write `Review: N/A — <reason>`. The numbers come from the reviewer's last response, not from your fix list — the parent uses this to tell "converged" from "fixed and not re-checked". **Any unresolved blocker means Verification cannot be PASS** — report FAIL (or BLOCKED if the reviewer could not be re-run) and repeat the blockers in the Warning line.

Mention command names, layer labels, reviewer implementation, simplify decisions, and detailed findings only when they failed, changed the result, exposed an unresolved material risk, or the parent asks. If either Tier 3 dimension was skipped or deferred, state which one and why.

## Anti-patterns

- **"Tests passed, skipping review"** — Dimension B is independently required. Tests verify runtime, not spec compliance or code quality.
- **Repeating the full protocol after every non-shipping phase** — verify once at the final cumulative release boundary.
- **Running L3 in the same context that wrote the code** — works for trivial changes, hides issues for anything subtle. Use the tool-selection table. (Dimension A only — Dimension B's review-loop is deliberately run in your own context, and finishes before L3 starts.)
- **Vague reports** ("looks good", "tests pass") — the parent needs concrete evidence per dimension.
- **Downgrading to `code-auditor` without a reason** — `review-loop` (B1) is the default; the fallback (B2) requires review-loop to be genuinely unavailable, stated in the report.
- **Fixing final-round blockers and declaring "all blockers resolved" without a confirm round** — a 6→3→3 trace followed by a fix is not convergence. Resolved is the reviewer's verdict, not yours; see the final-round rule and the mandatory `Review:` line.
- **Wrapping review-loop in a subagent, or forbidding it to fix** — each subagent starts a *new* Codex session, so round 2 has no memory of round 1 and re-reads the diff cold; the loop stops being a loop. Run review-loop inline and resume the same session (see Spawn budget).
- **Polling your own L3 subagent with `sleep` / `until` in Bash** — use the blocking `TaskOutput` tool and do nothing else; any code edit while L3 runs invalidates its verdict (see the required order). The poll only stalls.
- **Running simplify without the assessment gate, or after B / L3** — unconditional simplify wastes budget on mechanical diffs; simplify after B/L3 invalidates the review and E2E you just ran. Assess first, run between L2 and Dimension B, re-run L1+L2 if it changed anything. (The comment-only `deslop` pass after B is the deliberate exception — it is mandatory there, see the Deslop pass section.)
- **Skipping the post-review deslop because "I checked and there's no slop"** — that self-assessment is unreliable precisely where it matters: the fix rounds you just wrote are where the narration comes from. The pass is unconditional; only its report is optional.
- **Hand-rolling a browser E2E script for L3** (Puppeteer / Playwright / raw Chromium) — same-context script-writing is the self-verification trap wearing a browser costume. Use the driver-hint table (`e2e-dev-loop` / `agent-browser`).
- **L3 executor free-styling the observation instead of invoking the built-in `verify` skill** — without it you lose the probe requirement, evidence-capture rules, and strict verdict semantics; a happy-path replay with no 🔍 is not L3.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/pc035860/.claude/skills/review-loop

# Review Loop

## Overview

This skill enables continuous, automated code review and improvement cycles using Codex CLI, Opus 5.5 (`claude -p` isolated from user settings, as `opus`), Cursor (`cursor-agent` subagent: gpt-5.6-sol-medium or Grok 4.7), Antigravity (`agy-agent` subagent: Gemini 3.8 Flash), pi (`pi-agent` subagent: GLM 5.3 Flash as `glm` / DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as `ds`), or the code-auditor subagent — singly, or as the default `opus` + `glm` pair when the user asks for ensemble without naming tools. The loop automatically:
- Performs initial code/spec review
- Identifies blocking issues, suggestions, and decision points
- Fixes blocking issues that don't require user decisions
- Continues reviewing until clean or requires user input

**Core Features**: Automatic looping, cross-session support, intelligent interruption, progress tracking

**Script Location**: `scripts/` is in the same directory as this SKILL.md file. Reviews run from the *project* cwd, so a relative `scripts/…` path fails; use `SKILL_DIR="$HOME/.claude/skills/review-loop"` (or derive it from this file's location) and call `"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/<name>.sh"`. The docs' short `scripts/…` examples assume that substitution.

## Tool Selection

Choose your tool and **MUST read the corresponding `references/*-implementation.md` file** before proceeding. The implementation files contain critical setup and execution details that cannot be skipped:

**Fallback order (when the preferred tool is unavailable)**: Codex CLI → `cursor` (GPT 5.6 Sol via `cursor-agent` — Cursor has no gpt-6 yet) → code-auditor subagent. A failed `opus` run is not part of this chain — report it and offer `codex` or `glm` (see `claude-implementation.md`). Single-tool runs only — in Ensemble mode a dead reviewer is dropped, never substituted.

**Tool names the user may say** (aliases resolve to one route + one model; the shared task text lives in `references/review-prompt.md`):

| Name | Route | Model | Doc |
|------|-------|-------|-----|
| `codex` | `scripts/codex-review.sh` | gpt-6.1-sol | `codex-implementation.md` |
| `opus` / `claude` | `$HOME/.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/claude-review.sh` | `claude-opus-5-5`, effort high | `claude-implementation.md` |
| `cursor` | `cursor-agent` subagent | `gpt-5.6-sol-medium` | `cursor-implementation.md` |
| `grok` | `cursor-agent` subagent | `grok-4.7-high` | `cursor-implementation.md` |
| `agy` / `gemini` | `agy-agent` subagent | `gemini-3.8-flash-high` | `antigravity-implementation.md` |
| `pi` / `glm` | `pi-agent` subagent | `fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p3-flash` | `pi-implementation.md` |
| `ds` / `deepseek` | `pi-agent` subagent | `fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash-1017` | `pi-implementation.md` |
| `subagent` / `code-auditor` | `code-auditor` subagent | session model (not isolated — for Opus, say `opus`) | `subagent-implementation.md` |

**Runner unavailable → script fallback**: if the host has no `Agent` tool, or spawning returns `Agent type '<x>-agent' not found`, run the same route through its script (`scripts/pi-review.sh` / `cursor-review.sh` / `antigravity-review.sh`) with the same model and prompt. Only `pi-review.sh` can continue a subagent-started session; each doc's "Script fallback" section gives that route's handle.

**Two or more names in one request → Ensemble mode.** Same if the user asks for ensemble without naming tools (`review-loop ensemble`, `review-loop 用兩家`) — default pair is `opus` + `glm`. Read `references/ensemble-consolidation.md` in addition to each named tool's doc. Never fan out on a single named tool.

### Codex CLI
**Use when**: Codex CLI (`codex exec`) is installed. The wrapper locks in required parameters (`model`, `sandbox`, `reasoning_effort`, `reasoning_summary`) via explicit `-m / -s / -c` flags so they cannot drift through compaction — no user-side profile file required.

**Implementation**: Read `references/codex-implementation.md` for detailed steps

**Cursor agent only**: Cursor's Shell tool may background long commands before they finish. Read `references/codex-cursor-shell.md` before invoking `codex-review.sh` or `claude-review.sh` (same backgrounding; the `session_id` grep is codex-only).

### Opus (`opus` / `claude`)
**Use when**: quality matters most and the `claude` CLI is installed. Runs Opus 5.5 at effort `high` through the pr-review skill's `claude-review.sh`, isolated from every settings file, CLAUDE.md, hook, MCP server, and auto memory. Same wrapper and same model from Claude Code and Cursor. Session handle is `session key + cwd`; resume by re-running with the same `--key` / `--cwd`. Uses the user's Claude subscription.

**Implementation**: Read `references/claude-implementation.md` for detailed steps

### Cursor (`cursor` / `grok`)
**Use when**: `cursor-agent` is installed and the `cursor-agent` subagent is registered. `cursor` = `gpt-5.6-sol-medium`, the first fallback when Codex CLI is unavailable. `grok` = `grok-4.7-high`, the quality-first pick — highest-scoring reviewer of the set, but the slowest (~14 min on a large diff). Session handle is `session key + cwd + model`; resume by spawning `cursor-agent` again with the same header. Not from inside Cursor itself (see the doc).

**Implementation**: Read `references/cursor-implementation.md` for detailed steps

### Antigravity (`agy` / `gemini`)
**Use when**: Antigravity CLI installed and first-time interactive auth done; you want Gemini 3.8 Flash (~7 min on a large diff; mid-pack speed, and the one reviewer that has fabricated a supporting detail and over-ranked severities — better as an ensemble member than solo). Runs through the `agy-agent` subagent; session handle is `session key + cwd`, resumed by spawning `agy-agent` again with the same header. Override the model with `model: <id>` from `agy models`.

**Implementation**: Read `references/antigravity-implementation.md` for detailed steps

### Pi (`pi` / `glm` / `ds` / `deepseek`)
**Use when**: `pi` is installed with the fireworks provider and the `pi-agent` subagent is registered. Two named entries share this route and differ only in model — same shape as `cursor` / `grok`:

- `pi` / `glm` = GLM 5.3 Flash (precision / speed)
- `ds` / `deepseek` = DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (recall / schema-layer)

Effort `high`; session handle is `uuid5(cwd, key)`. `glm` and `ds` **must not share a session key** (the id does not include the model).

**Implementation**: Read `references/pi-implementation.md` for detailed steps

### Subagent (code-auditor)
**Use when**: Claude Code with Agent tool available, prefer native subagent over external tools, no Codex/Cursor/Antigravity setup. It runs with the global CLAUDE.md and graph-memory tools and was never benchmarked; when the user asks for Opus, use the `opus` route instead.

**Implementation**: Read `references/subagent-implementation.md` for detailed steps

**Fallback**: If `code-auditor` subagent is not available, use `generalPurpose` (or any general subagent) instead.

### Ensemble (`opus` + `glm` by default)
**Use when**: the user names two or more tools, **or** asks for ensemble without naming tools. Unnamed ensemble → `opus` + `glm` (costs Claude subscription usage — offer `ds` + `glm` when the user says usage is tight). Named tools override the default. All reviewers get the identical task text, run in parallel, and their findings are validated, deduped, tagged with consensus counts, and merged before Evaluation Logic. Each reviewer keeps its own session across rounds under a per-reviewer key derived from one run key.

**Implementation**: Read `references/ensemble-consolidation.md` (it references the sibling skill's `../interrogate/references/lead-judgment.md` for the filtering discipline, with an inline fallback if that skill is absent)

---

All routes share the same evaluation logic and termination conditions described below.

## Execution Context Detection

Before applying the main-agent vs subagent branches below, self-identify your execution context:

**You are a SUBAGENT if ANY of these signals apply:**
- System prompt mentions `caller`, `parent agent`, or phrases like "the caller will relay this to the user"
- `Task` / `Agent` tool is **not** available in your tool list
- You were invoked via another agent's Task/Agent call (no direct user chat history visible)

**Otherwise you are the MAIN AGENT** (direct user conversation; `Task`/`Agent` tool available).

When in doubt, treat "no `Task`/`Agent` tool available" as the authoritative signal.

## Common Loop Workflow

All tools follow the same review cycle:

```
Initial Review
  ↓
Save Session ID (any task-list tool; nested subagent → skip write, remember only)
  ↓
Validate Findings ──→ drop invalid; re-query ambiguous
  ↓
Evaluate Results ──→ No blocking? ──Yes→ Complete ✓
  ↓ No
Need decision? ──Yes→ [Context Gathering Flow]*
  ↓ No                      ↓
Fix Issues              Recommend
  ↓                         ↓
Continue Review         Ask User
  ↓                         ↓
Validate Findings ──┐   Pause ⏸️
  ↓                 │
Evaluate Results ───┘

* See references/context-gathering-guide.md
```

### Session ID persistence

After you obtain the session handle (Codex conversation/thread id; `session key + cwd` for `opus` and the cursor-agent / agy-agent / pi-agent routes, plus the model for cursor-agent and pi-agent; subagent `agentId`; in Ensemble mode the run key plus every reviewer's handle):

- **Main agent** (see Execution Context Detection) — Persist it with **whatever task-list affordance** the host exposes. Pick one mechanism; the goal is a durable reminder for multi-step follow-ups, without assuming a fixed tool schema.
- **Subagent** (see Execution Context Detection) — **Do not** write to the shared task list (subagents share the parent pool; extra items pollute or race). **Still retain the id in working memory** and pass it into the next continue step within that same run (each route's resume mechanism is in its `*-implementation.md`).

## Validate Review Results

⚠️ **Run after every review (initial and `Continue Review`), before Evaluation Logic.**

Reviewer findings are not always actionable: they may be false positives, reflect a different perspective from the project's actual intent or constraints, or — after `--resume` — reference stale context. Treat every finding as unverified until the main agent confirms it directly against the source and the project's intent.

For each blocking issue and suggestion:
1. Read the cited `file:line`
2. Confirm the file and line range exist
3. Confirm the code at that location matches the reviewer's description
4. Confirm the issue actually applies there

Outcomes:
- **Valid** → keep; flows into Evaluation Logic
- **Invalid** (path/line wrong, code mismatch, issue does not apply) → drop the finding; never enter Fix Issues for it
- **Ambiguous** (partial match, scope unclear) → re-query the same reviewer session through that route's resume mechanism (see its `*-implementation.md`) for clarification before deciding

Only validated findings reach Situation A / B / C.

## Evaluation Logic

After each review, evaluate results using this decision tree:

### Situation A - No Blocking Issues
**Action**: End loop ✓
- All critical issues resolved
- Code meets quality standards

### Situation B - Requires User Decision
**Action**: Context Check → Explore (if needed) → Recommend → Pause ⏸️

Before asking the user, ensure sufficient context:
1. Check if context is sufficient to provide informed recommendations
2. If insufficient, gather context using Explore agent
3. Provide recommendation with collected context
4. Then ask user for decision

**Implementation**: Read `references/context-gathering-guide.md` for detailed steps

**When to trigger**:
- Architecture design choices
- Feature scope definition
- Technology stack selection
- Business logic decisions
- Security trade-offs

### Situation C - Auto-Fixable Issues
**Action**: Continue to fix issues
**When**:
- Syntax/type errors
- Logic errors
- Style violations
- Performance optimizations
- Naming conventions

Fix only clear, non-decision issues, then continue review cycle.

## Termination Conditions

### Complete Termination ✓
- No blocking issues remain
- Code meets quality standards
- All auto-fixable issues resolved

### Pause Termination ⏸️
- User decision required
- Architecture/feature/technology choices needed
- Cannot proceed without business logic input

## Quick Reference

### Scripts Available
- **Codex**: `scripts/codex-review.sh` — wraps `codex exec` with locked `model=gpt-6.1-sol / sandbox=workspace-write / reasoning_effort=medium / reasoning_summary=auto`, all applied via `-m / -s / -c`. After every run the wrapper emits `✨ session_id=<UUID>` on stderr — grep that line to capture the UUID. Use `--resume <UUID>` for follow-up rounds.
- **Opus**: `$HOME/.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/claude-review.sh --key … --effort high --cwd …` (prompt on stdin) — no `--model`: the wrapper defaults to `claude-opus-5-5`; isolation is fixed inside it. Resume = re-run with the same `--key` + `--cwd`; the stderr trailer `✨ session_key=… session_id=… cwd=…` confirms the handle.
- **Cursor / Grok**: Agent tool with `subagent_type=cursor-agent`; header `session key:` + `model:` (`gpt-5.6-sol-medium` for `cursor`, `grok-4.7-high` for `grok` — always explicit, the wrapper default is Grok). Resume = respawn with the same header, not `SendMessage`. Fallback `scripts/cursor-review.sh --model <id> <CHAT_ID>` (Cursor host, or subagent unavailable).
- **Antigravity**: Agent tool with `subagent_type=agy-agent`; header `session key:` (+ optional `model:`). Resume = respawn with the same header. Fallback `scripts/antigravity-review.sh` (its own conversation, not the subagent's — see doc).
- **Pi**: Agent tool with `subagent_type=pi-agent`; header `session key:` / `model:` (`fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p3-flash` for `glm`, `…/deepseek-v4p1-flash-1017` for `ds`) / `effort: high`. Resume = respawn with the same key + cwd + model. Fallback `scripts/pi-review.sh --key … --model … --cwd …` derives the same session id.
- **Wrapper subagent routes** (`cursor-agent` / `agy-agent` / `pi-agent`): add `cwd: /abs/path` to the header when the target repo differs from the session cwd (a parsed wrapper parameter — see `references/review-prompt.md`).
- **Every route** (codex, opus, and code-auditor included): the task text is copied verbatim from `references/review-prompt.md`.
- **Subagent**: Agent tool with `subagent_type=code-auditor` (fallback: `generalPurpose`), save `agentId` for resume
- **Ensemble**: default pair `opus` + `glm` when the user asks for ensemble without names; otherwise the named tools. Run key `review-<scope>-<timestamp>`, per-reviewer key `<run key>-<canonical>` (`pi`→`glm`, `deepseek`→`ds`; same route + same model collapse). Spawn all in one message; consolidate per `references/ensemble-consolidation.md`

### Must Pause For
- Architecture decisions
- Feature scope
- Technology choices
- Business logic
- Security trade-offs

### Can Auto-Handle
- Syntax errors
- Type errors
- Style issues
- Simple optimizations
- Naming conventions

### Self-Check Before Loop
- [ ] Defined review completion criteria?
- [ ] Clarified pause decision points?
- [ ] Prepared project path?
- [ ] Selected appropriate tool (codex / opus / cursor / grok / agy / glm / ds / subagent)? Ensemble if the user named ≥2 **or** asked for ensemble (default `opus` + `glm`)?

### Self-Check After Each Review (before Evaluation)
- [ ] Read every finding's cited `file:line`?
- [ ] Dropped findings whose code doesn't match the reviewer's description?
- [ ] Re-queried reviewer for ambiguous findings?
- [ ] Ensemble: deduped across reviewers, consensus counts attached, disagreements listed, dropped reviewers named?

### Self-Check During Evaluation
- [ ] Any blocking issues?
- [ ] Requires user decision?
- [ ] Can auto-fix?

### Self-Check Before Loop End
- [ ] All blocking issues fixed?
- [ ] Session ID persisted or held in memory (first time)? Task-list write skipped when running as subagent — see Execution Context Detection (Codex: conversation/thread id; opus: session key + cwd; cursor-agent / pi-agent: session key + cwd + model; agy-agent: session key + cwd; Subagent: agentId; Ensemble: run key + per-reviewer handles)
- [ ] Fixes documented?

# Codex Implementation Guide

This guide provides detailed steps for using the Review Loop with **Codex CLI headless mode** (`codex exec`), wrapped by `scripts/codex-review.sh`. The wrapper hard-codes the required parameters via explicit `-m / -s / -c` flags so they cannot drift across compactions or sessions — and so the wrapper does not depend on any user-side profile file existing.

## Prerequisites

- `codex` CLI installed (`codex --version` should return ≥ 0.122.0). Any official install method works:
  - `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh` (Mac/Linux shell installer)
  - `brew install --cask codex` (Homebrew)
  - `npm install -g @openai/codex` (npm — with or without nvm)
  - GitHub Releases binary from <https://github.com/openai/codex/releases>
- Logged in (`codex login`)
- `scripts/codex-review.sh` is executable

The wrapper auto-detects how to invoke codex:

1. **`codex` on PATH** (preferred) — covers brew, shell installer, direct binary, and npm installs whose default Node version is active.
2. **`nvm exec default codex`** (fallback) — only used when codex isn't on PATH but nvm is available: the shell's active Node (e.g. a project `.nvmrc` pinning Node 12) lacks codex. It targets nvm's `default` alias, the same Node a fresh shell would use.
3. **Neither** — the script exits with a clear list of supported install methods.

The wrapper has no dependency on `~/.codex/mcp.config.toml` or any `[profiles.*]` section — every required setting is applied explicitly on each invocation.

## Locked Parameters (Handled by the Wrapper)

The wrapper script hard-codes the parameters that silently degrade review quality when omitted. All four are applied via explicit flags / `-c` overrides on **both** initial and resume runs, so they cannot drift even if user config changes:

| Parameter                   | Locked Value      | How it's applied                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `model`                     | `gpt-6.1-sol`       | `-m gpt-6.1-sol`                                                                                         |
| `sandbox`                   | `workspace-write` | `-s workspace-write` (initial) / `-c sandbox_mode="workspace-write"` (resume — `-s` not accepted) |
| `model_reasoning_effort`    | `medium`          | `-c model_reasoning_effort="medium"`                                                                   |
| `model_reasoning_summary`   | `auto`            | `-c model_reasoning_summary="auto"`                                                                    |

You cannot override these via the wrapper — that is intentional. If you ever need different values, invoke `codex exec` directly rather than editing the wrapper.

## Step 1: Initial Review

**IMPORTANT**: Set Bash timeout dynamically based on visible review scope — `600000ms` (10 min) baseline for small/single-file reviews, up to `1200000ms` (20 min) for large or complex reviews (multi-file specs, deep exploration).

Use the wrapper script with a heredoc for the review prompt. The prompt body is the matching **Spec/Plan** or **Code** block from `references/review-prompt.md`, copied verbatim — codex must see the same task text as every other route, or ensemble consensus means nothing. Reviews run from the *project* cwd, so resolve the script path from this skill's directory rather than typing `scripts/…` relative:

```bash
SKILL_DIR="$HOME/.claude/skills/review-loop"     # derive from this SKILL.md's location if installed elsewhere
"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/codex-review.sh" --cwd /path/to/project <<'PROMPT'
<task text — Spec/Plan or Code block from review-prompt.md>
PROMPT
```

The examples below keep the short `scripts/codex-review.sh` form for readability; substitute `"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/codex-review.sh"` when you run them.

### Alternative Input Methods

The wrapper supports positional argument, pipe, and heredoc:

```bash
# Positional
scripts/codex-review.sh "short review prompt"

# Pipe
cat prompt.txt | scripts/codex-review.sh

# Heredoc (recommended for multi-line review prompts)
scripts/codex-review.sh <<'PROMPT'
... multi-line ...
PROMPT
```

## Step 2: Capture the Session ID

The wrapper emits a machine-readable trailer on **stderr** after every run:

```
✨ session_id=019db489-cb91-7680-bcc5-907fdba8a77e
```

Extract it by capturing stderr and grepping:

```bash
scripts/codex-review.sh --cwd /path/to/project "review prompt" 2>/tmp/cr.err
SID=$(grep -m1 '^✨ session_id=' /tmp/cr.err | cut -d= -f2)
```

The same UUID also appears in the Codex header line `session id: <UUID>` that the wrapper relays alongside the streamed output, but the stderr trailer is intended as the canonical, scriptable capture point.

If the trailer line reads `⚠️ 無法從 codex 輸出抓到 session id...` instead of `✨ session_id=

- `UV_PYTHON_CACHE_DIR`（若用到 managed Python）：Python 安裝 archive 的 cache

範例（在 Prompt 中指示 Codex 執行時）：

```bash

```

### Error Handling

If the review fails, check in this order:

1. Is `codex --version` runnable directly from your shell? If yes, the wrapper takes the PATH branch. If no, check the npm-under-nvm fallback: codex installed via `npm install -g @openai/codex` on a non-default Node version is only reachable through `nvm exec`. Ensure `~/.nvm/nvm.sh` exists — the wrapper loads it automatically and runs `nvm exec default codex`.
2. `The '<model>' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account` — the wrapper prints the codex version that actually ran. An old codex-cli is the usual cause; otherwise check `codex app-server daemon version` (CLI and daemon versions should match) and the ChatGPT plan (openai/codex#49396).
3. Is the user logged in? `codex login` (session stored in `~/.codex/auth.json`)
4. Did you set the Bash tool timeout in the `600000-1200000ms` (10-20 min) range, scaled to review scope?
5. For `--resume` errors (`session not found`): verify the UUID is correct, session files live under `~/.codex/sessions/` — they are not deleted automatically.

### Manual Execution (Not Recommended)

If you need to bypass the wrapper (e.g., to use a different sandbox or model), the equivalent raw commands are:

```bash
# New review
codex exec \
    -m gpt-6.1-sol \
    -s workspace-write \
    -C /path/to/project \
    -c 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"' \
    -c 'model_reasoning_summary="auto"' \
    "prompt" </dev/null

# Resume — must replicate the wrapper's compensations or settings will drift:
( cd /path/to/project && \
  codex exec resume \
      -m gpt-6.1-sol \
      -c 'sandbox_mode="workspace-write"' \
      -c 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"' \
      -c 'model_reasoning_summary="auto"' \
      <UUID> "prompt" </dev/null )
```

Note the `</dev/null` — without it, Codex prints `Reading additional input from stdin...` and appends any stray stdin to the prompt.

`codex exec resume` does not accept `-s / -C`. Skipping the `-c` overrides above causes review quality to silently degrade (sandbox falls back to your `~/.codex/config.toml` default, reasoning effort/summary drop to whatever the base config sets).

## Next Steps

After completing Step 3, return to the **Evaluation Logic** section in the main SKILL.md to determine:

- Whether to end the loop (no blocking issues)
- Whether to pause (requires user decision)
- Whether to continue (more auto-fixable issues)

|-------------|------------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Session handle | UUID (from header)  | derived `uuid5(cwd, key)`       | conv id cached by cwd + session key        | chat id cached by cwd + session key     | derived `uuid5(cwd, key)`      |

| Persistence | `~/.codex/sessions/`   | `~/.claude/projects/`           | `~/.cache/agy-agent-wrapper/sessions/`     | `~/.cache/cursor-agent-wrapper/sessions/` | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`      |

# Shared Review Prompt

The task text handed to every reviewer, regardless of route. Keeping it byte-identical across
tools is what makes their findings comparable (and what makes ensemble consensus meaningful).
The subagent routes (`cursor-agent`, `agy-agent`, `pi-agent`) prepend their parameter header
lines to this text; the script routes (`codex-review.sh`, `claude-review.sh` for `opus`, and the per-route fallback scripts) pass it as the prompt body.

## `cwd:` header line (subagent routes only)

The three wrapper subagents (`cursor-agent`, `agy-agent`, `pi-agent`) run in the main session's
cwd and derive their session cache / session id from it. When the review target lives in another
repo, add a `cwd:` line to the parameter header, next to `session key:` / `model:`:

```
cwd: /abs/path/to/project
```

It is a parsed parameter of all three wrappers (see their agent definitions); they `cd` there
before computing the handle, so the session handle is `key + that cwd`. Omit it when the target is
the current project — and once used, repeat the identical line on every continue round, or the
resume lands in a different cache bucket.

## For Spec/Plan Files

Use when reviewing files with names containing `spec`, `plan`, or `design`:

```
Review this spec/plan thoroughly: <file paths or description>. Do NOT modify any files; this is a read-only review.

## Output Contract
Respond in exactly this section order:
1. **Blocking Issues** (must fix) — format: `[file:line]` issue — impact
2. **Suggestions** (non-blocking improvements) — format: `[file:line]` suggestion — rationale
3. **Questions** (require user decision) — format: question — why decision is needed
4. **Summary** (1-2 sentences on overall readiness)

## Review Focus
1. Completeness: Are all relevant files listed? How do parts collaborate/integrate?
2. Feasibility: Are implementation steps clear and executable? Are dependencies explicit?
3. Coherence: Is the path from current state to goal state complete?
4. MVP Principles: Any over-engineering? Is the core function clearly scoped?

## Execution Rules
- Read ALL relevant files before reporting; maintain an internal checklist of files to review
- Base every issue on retrieved file content only — never fabricate problems
- Cite exact file:line for each finding; mark blocked items with what information is missing
- Continue reading files until the review is complete; retry with different search strategies if results are empty
- Verify each issue before reporting: does the problem actually exist at that location?
- Do NOT spawn subagents or trigger additional review rounds — complete your entire review in a single response
```

## For Code Files

```
Review <describe content, e.g. "merge commit abc123 — start with `git diff abc123^1 abc123`"> thoroughly. Do NOT modify any files; this is a read-only review.

## Output Contract
Respond in exactly this section order:
1. **Blocking Issues** (must fix) — format: `[file:line]` issue — impact
2. **Suggestions** (non-blocking improvements) — format: `[file:line]` suggestion — rationale
3. **Questions** (require user decision) — format: question — why decision is needed
4. **Summary** (1-2 sentences on overall code quality)

## Review Focus
1. Code quality and maintainability
2. Potential bugs or logic errors
3. Performance and security considerations

## Execution Rules
- Read ALL relevant files before reporting; maintain an internal checklist
- Base every finding on retrieved code only — never fabricate issues
- Cite exact file:line for each finding; mark blocked items with what information is missing
- Continue reading files until the review is complete; retry with different strategies if results are empty
- Verify each issue: confirm the problem exists at the cited location before reporting
- Do NOT spawn subagents or trigger additional review rounds — complete your entire review in a single response
```

## Continue Review (after fixes)

Same session handle as the initial round (see each route's doc for what "same handle" means):

```
Fixed:
1. <fix>
2. <fix>

Please continue review. Same output contract: Blocking Issues → Suggestions → Questions → Summary.
Verify the above fixes are actually applied before reporting new issues.
Do NOT spawn subagents or trigger additional review rounds — complete your entire review in a single response.
```

## Persona bleed

`cursor-agent` inherits the user's global Cursor persona; `agy` and `pi` read the user's global
CLAUDE.md / output-style. Some models echo that persona into the review prose. It does not affect
findings — strip it before pasting a review anywhere external. If a neutral voice matters, add one
line to the task text: `Respond in plain technical English; no persona.`
